findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still abstract and will crash when instantiated
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler requires implementations of counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. MetricAlertDetectorHandler only contains pass, so it remains abstract. Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector using this type will raise TypeError instead of being evaluated.

findings.title: get_state_data crashes for stateful detectors with no counters
findings.body: If a StatefulDetectorHandler defines an empty counter_names list, the `if self.counter_names:` block is skipped and `counter_updates` remains an empty dict. The later `counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]` raises KeyError for every group key. The method should default to an empty dict per group key when there are no counters.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but the docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. This can mislead implementers and callers.

findings.title: Produced occurrences will always use hardcoded project_id 1
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler now builds IssueOccurrence and StatusChangeMessage using self.detector.project_id, but Detector.project_id is a temporary property that always returns 1. If this code path is enabled for real detectors, issues and status changes will be associated with the wrong project.

findings.title: test_dedupe expects an occurrence for the wrong group key
findings.body: The test builds the expected occurrence for group key 'val1' but then evaluates and asserts a DetectorEvaluationResult for group key 'group_key'. The actual handler will build an occurrence/fingerprint for 'group_key', so the assertion is either wrong or fails to verify the correct fingerprint. The helper should be called with 'group_key'.
